_comment: Accepted accessibility violations. tools/a11y_check.py reports every entry
here on every run and does not fail on it; anything NOT here fails the run.
This is a ledger, not a mute. Each entry is printed with its reason on each
run, and the checker warns when an entry stops matching anything so a fixed
one does not sit here forever pretending to be a known problem.
Both current entries are third-party markup this repo does not author. An
entry that describes this site's own HTML or CSS does not belong here -- fix
it instead. Nothing here licenses a conformance claim; see the header of

accepted.reason: Quarto's own Bootstrap navbar template renders the mobile toggle as <button class='navbar-toggler' role='menu'> with no menuitem children. It is generated by `quarto render` from the theme, not written here, so it cannot be fixed in this repo without patching Quarto's output. Affects the mobile viewport on every page. Revisit on a Quarto upgrade.

MathJax emits <mjx-speech aria-roledescription='' aria-braillelabel='...'> in its accessibility layer on the sibling-conflict paper, the one page carrying rendered mathematics. The empty aria-roledescription is MathJax's, and aria-braillelabel is a genuine ARIA attribute this axe build does not yet recognise. Removing MathJax would cost the page its equations and its speech text, which is a net accessibility loss.
accepted.intermittent_reason: MathJax builds its speech layer asynchronously after load, so this matches on some runs and not others. Exempt from the stale-entry warning for that reason and no other.

accepted_reflow.reason: Retired build. The portfolio deliberately keeps completed work as it shipped, because the progression across builds is part of what it is showing -- reflowing an old page would edit that record. Overflow is a custom 860 px roadmap diagram (.bmg-goal, .bmg-months) with no scroll container -- a different defect from the table case and a larger fix, the same defect fixed on cascadia.html and cascadia-controltower.html; the fix is a `::: {.table-scroll}` wrapper and the CSS already ships. Apply it if this build is ever put back in front of an interviewer.
